title: IdentityLink
description: A claim that two identifiers refer to the same thing, or that one came from the other. Links are how codes get joined at each handoff: whoever holds two codes at the same moment (exporter, importer, roaster) records one link, and the registry assembles the chain. Nobody has to join the whole supply chain.

relation.description: sameAs: two codes for the same thing. derivedFrom: 'from' was made from 'to' (a roast batch from a green lot). partOf: 'from' is a portion of 'to' (a split lot). mergedInto: duplicate records merged; 'to' is canonical.

confidence.description: confirmed: asserted by a party who held both codes, or by the subject. probable: suggested by matching (same origin, crop year, weight, timing) and awaiting confirmation.

evidence.description: Where the two codes appeared together, e.g. contract, invoice, warehouse receipt, bag stencil, matching rule.

ref.description: Either an Open Parchment id, or an outside identifier.
